title: rms

gpu_support.notes: GPU inputs are gathered to host for compatibility until provider reduction hooks exist.

description: `rms(X)` computes `sqrt(mean(abs(X).^2))` along the first non-singleton dimension. Dimension, vector-dimension, `"all"`, `"includenan"`, `"omitnan"`, `"includemissing"`, and `"omitmissing"` forms are supported.
behaviors: `"omitnan"` skips NaNs in each slice; empty slices return `NaN`.
Logical and integer inputs are promoted to double precision before reduction.
Complex inputs are reduced using magnitude.

examples.description: Root mean square of a vector

faqs.question: Is rms the same as norm divided by sqrt(n)?
faqs.answer: For a vector without omitted values, yes: `rms(x)` equals `norm(x)/sqrt(numel(x))`.
